talks.teaser: Shares firsthand experiences navigating vulnerability disclosure programs in the aviation industry, highlighting common pitfalls and best practices.
talks.summary:
Vulnerability Disclosure Dynamics in Aviation

Vulnerability Disclosure Programs (VDPs) in the aviation sector operate under intense regulatory scrutiny and safety sensitivities, creating friction between independent researchers and aircraft manufacturers.

Firsthand Perspectives from Submissions and Triage

Matt Gaffney shares real-world case studies from both submitting and receiving vulnerability disclosures within the aerospace industry, illustrating how bureaucratic delays and legal threats undermine constructive security research.

Common Institutional Pitfalls

Key shortcomings include ambiguous scope definitions, defensive legal posturing, failure to provide receipt acknowledgments, and lack of safe harbor protections for good-faith researchers.

Frameworks for Constructive Aerospace VDPs

Improving aviation vulnerability handling requires adopting standardized ISO/IEC 29147 disclosure practices, establishing dedicated aerospace CERT channels, and fostering open dialogue with the research community.

talks.title: Vulns to End Your Space Mission
talks.teaser: Demonstrates proof-of-concept exploits across ground control software and onboard satellite components that grant unauthorized spacecraft control.
talks.summary:
Expanding Attack Surfaces in Space Missions

Modern space missions integrate specialized hardware and software components communicating across custom ground-to-space protocols. Vulnerabilities anywhere in this chain can result in total mission loss.

Vulnerability Analysis of Ground Control Segments

Researchers identified critical flaws across ground station control software, telemetry servers, and antenna controllers, enabling unauthenticated remote command injection into satellite uplinks.

Exploiting Onboard Spacecraft Firmware

Inspecting onboard spacecraft software revealed memory corruption bugs and unauthenticated debugging interfaces in flight computers. Proof-of-concept exploits demonstrated the ability to hijack attitude control and disrupt satellite subsystems.

Hardening Guidelines for Aerospace Missions

Securing space infrastructure requires end-to-end cryptographic command authentication, memory-safe flight software architectures, and rigorous penetration testing before launch.

talks.title: Hacking Space to Defend It: Generating IoBs with SPARTA
talks.teaser: Applies offensive techniques from the SPARTA framework to generate behavioral indicators (IoBs) and design realistic intrusion detection systems for spacecraft.
talks.summary:
The Need for Threat-Informed Space Defense

While the SPARTA (Space Attack Research and Tactic Analysis) framework cataloged spaceborne cyber threats, mission operators needed empirical methods to detect these attacks in operational environments.

Simulating Space Attacks and TTP Replay

Brandon Bailey details hands-on offensive testing against simulated spacecraft flight software and telemetry buses to observe behavioral anomalies and telemetry patterns generated during active attacks.

Generating Indicators of Behavior (IoBs)

From these simulations, researchers developed concrete Indicators of Behavior (IoBs)—such as unexpected CPU scheduling spikes, anomalous telemetry packet rates, and out-of-sequence command verifications—tailored to resource-constrained flight computers.

Designing Spaceborne Intrusion Detection Systems

Integrating data-driven IoBs into spacecraft IDS architectures enables real-time threat detection aboard satellites without overloading onboard computing resources.

talks.title: Creating a Virtual Ship Environment Optimized for Cybersecurity Use
talks.teaser: Explores the architecture of a hybrid virtual ship simulator augmented with marine engine and instrument emulators for maritime security research.
talks.summary:
Limitations of Standard Maritime Simulators

Commercial maritime simulators are designed to train deck officers for navigational certifications (STCW) and lack the underlying network architectures necessary for cybersecurity assessments and research.

Hybrid Virtual Ship Architecture

Jeff Greer presents research from UNCW establishing a hybrid virtual ship environment that integrates full-mission bridge simulations with specialized hardware emulators and virtualized industrial controllers.

Simulating Engine Controls and Bridge Instruments

By augmenting commercial simulators (such as the Unitest Winterthur X92 marine engine simulator) with virtualized CAN and NMEA interfaces, researchers can inject cyberattacks and observe realistic physical vessel responses.

Applications in Education and Security Research

The hybrid testbed provides a safe, reproducible environment for training maritime defenders, testing intrusion detection algorithms, and evaluating shipboard cyber resilience.

talks.title: Bio Cryptography is the Game Genie in a post quantum dystopia
talks.teaser: Explores bio-cryptography and biological key generation as decentralized cryptographic primitives resilient against post-quantum computational attacks.
talks.summary:
Post-Quantum Cryptographic Vulnerabilities

As quantum computing advances threaten standard asymmetric encryption algorithms, researchers are exploring biological and physiological data sources to generate dynamic, decentralized cryptographic keys.

Principles of Bio-Cryptography

Bio-cryptography combines unique, high-entropy biological signals (such as genomic sequences or dynamic physiological metrics) with error-correcting codes to derive reproducible cryptographic keying material.

Decentralized Key Derivation and Verification

By grounding key generation in biological processes, systems eliminate centralized key escrow and static credential storage, creating self-sovereign authentication mechanisms resistant to quantum cryptanalysis.

Ethical Considerations and Future Applications

Deploying bio-cryptographic primitives requires addressing biological data privacy, template protection, and ensuring ethical boundaries in biometric security deployments.

talks.title: Evolution of Drain Attacks
talks.teaser: Traces the evolution of wallet draining attacks across Ethereum, Solana, and TON, demonstrating token spoofing exploits and transaction tracking methods.
talks.summary:
The Mechanics of Cryptocurrency Wallet Drainers

Wallet draining attacks represent one of the most widespread financial fraud vectors in the Web3 ecosystem, targeting cryptocurrency holders across Ethereum, Solana, and TON blockchains.

Evolution from Approval Abuse to Token Spoofing

Early drainers relied on deceptive ERC-20 'setApprovalForAll' contract calls. Modern drainer kits employ sophisticated token spoofing, off-chain signature manipulation (such as Permit and Permit2 abuse), and multi-chain transaction batching.

Laundering Networks and Illicit Flow Tracking

Analyzing blockchain transaction graphs reveals how drainer operators move stolen assets through cross-chain bridges, decentralized mixers, and money laundering funnels to cash out proceeds.

Wallet Security and Defensive Monitoring

Mitigating drainer attacks requires wallet interfaces to provide human-readable transaction simulation, revoke dormant contract allowances, and flag known phishing domains.

talks.title: Unveiling IoT Vulns: From Backdoors to Bureaucracy
talks.teaser: Examines over 50 real-world IoT vulnerability cases featuring hardcoded backdoors and discusses systemic barriers in reporting flaws to vendors and CERTs.
talks.summary:
Widespread Vulnerabilities in the IoT Ecosystem

Analyzing over 50 real-world IoT vulnerability disclosures reveals persistent systemic security flaws across commercial routers, industrial cameras, and environmental monitoring devices.

Hardcoded Backdoors and Predictable Credentials

Critical vulnerabilities, including CVE-2024-48271 (CVSS 9.8) and CVE-2025-1143, demonstrate vendor-embedded backdoors, hardcoded root credentials, and unauthenticated management consoles that grant remote attackers global device control.

Risks to Critical Infrastructure

Poorly secured commercial IoT devices deployed in municipal water plants, ATM networks, and transportation systems provide direct pivot points for criminal scammers and nation-state threat actors.

Bureaucratic Barriers in Responsible Disclosure

Kai-Ching Wang and Chiao-Lin Yu share the challenges of navigating vendor denials, unresponsive CNAs, and multi-year reporting delays, advocating for reforms in international vulnerability coordination.

talks.title: The PowerPoint Glove
talks.teaser: Walks through hacking the retro NES Power Glove with an ESP32 microcontroller to build a custom Bluetooth presentation controller.
talks.summary:
Hacking Retro Gaming Accessories

The iconic Nintendo Power Glove, released for the NES in 1989, remains a beloved cult accessory. Modern microcontrollers allow enthusiasts to repurpose its sensors for practical computing tasks.

Reverse Engineering the NES Controller Protocol

Parsia Hakimian breaks down the proprietary shift register communication protocol used by the original NES controller port, explaining how flex sensors and keypad buttons report physical state.

Interfacing with the ESP32 Microcontroller

Wiring the Power Glove to an ESP32 development board enables reading button scancodes and flex sensor resistance in real time, translating gestures and button presses into standard HID keyboard commands.

Building a Wireless Bluetooth Presentation Tool

Configuring the ESP32 as a Bluetooth HID device turns the Power Glove into an interactive PowerPoint remote controller, demonstrating accessible microcontroller hacking for conference presentations.

talks.title: Cloned Vishing : A case study
talks.teaser: Presents empirical results from a university research study evaluating user vulnerability and defensive safeguards against AI voice-cloned vishing attacks.
talks.summary:
Social Engineering and Human-Oriented Security

This presentation explores social engineering attacks and human vulnerability in security systems. Topics include psychological manipulation, pretexting, credential harvesting, and how attackers exploit human nature to bypass technical defenses.

talks.title: The Missing Link: Draytek’s New RCEs Complete the Chain
talks.teaser: Discloses two unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerabilities in Draytek routers (CVE-2024-51138 and CVE-2024-51139) that enable full edge device takeovers.
talks.summary:
Edge Router Vulnerabilities in Corporate Networks

Draytek routers are widely deployed as edge gateways across enterprise and small business networks. Their internet-exposed management interfaces make them prime targets for botnets and state-sponsored threat actors.

Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution Flaws

Researchers disclose two critical zero-day vulnerabilities in Draytek firmware: CVE-2024-51138 (a buffer overflow in STUN CGI handling) and CVE-2024-51139 (an integer overflow in CGI query parsing).

End-to-End Exploitation and Persistence Chain

Chaining these RCE vulnerabilities with previously documented firmware persistence techniques allows unauthenticated attackers to achieve root access from the WAN interface and install persistent backdoors.

Tooling and Edge Device Defense

The researchers release Draytek Arsenal, an open-source firmware analysis toolkit, emphasizing the necessity of rapid edge device patching and disabling external management interfaces.

talks.title: Vibe School: Making dumb devices smart with AI
talks.teaser: Demonstrates using AI-assisted coding to reverse engineer conventional hardware and integrate legacy sensors into Home Assistant.
talks.summary:
Democratizing Smart Home Integration with AI

Commercial smart home sensors and specialized environmental monitors often carry high prices, while inexpensive conventional hardware lacks network connectivity. AI-assisted programming lowers the barrier to bridging legacy hardware into modern smart home platforms.

Sniffing Sensor Signals and Protocol Analysis

Katie Paxton Fear demonstrates how to intercept and decode communication signals from an inexpensive conventional weather station using basic hardware sniffers and radio receivers.

AI-Assisted Microcontroller Firmware Development

Using generative AI models (such as Gemini) to write C++ firmware for microcontrollers (ESP32 / Arduino), researchers rapidly translate raw sensor telemetry into structured MQTT payloads.

Integrating Legacy Hardware into Home Assistant

Connecting the custom firmware to Home Assistant creates an automated, low-cost smart weather station, illustrating how 'vibe coding' empowers makers to customize connected devices.

talks.title: The Things know What You Did Last Session
talks.teaser: Examines corporate threat investigations, from detecting robotic fingerprint timecard fraud to uncovering remote North Korean IT contractor networks.
talks.summary:
Investigating Physical and Digital Enterprise Threats

Corporate threat investigations routinely span physical hardware manipulation, digital forensics, and international cybercrime schemes. Investigator Will Baggett shares real-world case studies from complex internal inquiries.

Automated Hardware Timecard Fraud

In a bizarre fraud scheme, an on-site contractor engineered a robotic device with synthetic flesh to automatically press a biometric fingerprint reader daily on a hidden iPhone, faking physical attendance on corporate visitor networks.

Chip-Off Extraction of Voting Machine Hardware

Baggett details IoT forensic investigations involving chip-off flash memory extraction from prototype voting machines, demonstrating hardware extraction techniques used for national security assessments.

Hunting North Korean IT Worker Fraud Networks

Investigating remote IT contractor networks revealed North Korean operatives utilizing piKVM switches, VPN routers, and virtual machine tunneling to bypass enterprise identity verification and funnel earnings back to DPRK state operations.

Forensic Indicators and Mitigation Strategies

Detecting contractor fraud requires correlating network telemetry, analyzing device fingerprints, monitoring anomalous VPN connections, and conducting rigorous identity verification interviews.

talks.title: Access Control Done Right the First Time
talks.teaser: Provides practical engineering best practices for deploying physical access control systems, covering supervised wiring, tamper resistance, and badge encryption.
talks.summary:
Pitfalls of Minimum Viable Access Control

Physical Access Control Systems (PACS) are frequently installed using minimum viable product configurations that leave doors vulnerable to simple physical bypasses and electronic credential cloning.

Supervised Wiring and Tamper Resistance

Tim Clevenger explains the critical importance of supervised reader wiring and end-of-line resistors, which detect when cables are cut or spliced by physical red teamers attempting inline badge cloning.

Selecting Clone-Resistant Credentials

Replacing vulnerable legacy 125 kHz proximity cards (such as standard HID Prox) with modern encrypted smartcards (like MIFARE DESFire EV3 or HID Seos) prevents unauthorized badge duplication.

Hardening Controllers and Operational Maintenance

Securing access control infrastructure requires locking controller enclosures, isolating management networks, maintaining accurate badge revocation records, and routinely testing door position switches.

talks.title: Smart Devices, Dumb Resets:Testing Firmware Persistence in Commercial IoT
talks.teaser: Investigates retail returns sanitization, proving that modified IoT firmware persists across store resales and creates supply chain backdoor vectors.
talks.summary:
Supply Chain Vulnerabilities in Returned Retail Electronics

Consumer electronics retailers routinely process returned smart home devices and resell them as open-box or refurbished goods. However, retailer sanitization and reset procedures are rarely audited for cybersecurity risks.

Experimental Methodology: Planting Custom Firmware

Matei Jose purchased commercial IoT devices from major retail stores, flashed custom firmware embedding a persistent callback beacon, and returned the products following standard return procedures.

Persistence Across Retail Restocking Pipelines

Repurchasing the returned items revealed that major retailers failed to properly wipe or reflash device firmware, allowing custom backdoor firmware to remain fully intact and operational.

Risks of Retail Supply Chain Implants

This sanitization failure creates a viable attack vector for adversaries to deploy persistent IoT botnet implants, exfiltration tools, or surveillance backdoors directly into consumer supply chains.

Mitigation Strategies for Manufacturers and Retailers

Addressing retail supply chain persistence requires manufacturers to implement cryptographic firmware attestation, enforce hardware-level factory reset fuses, and mandate automated retailer device sanitization.

talks.title: Incident Response from a Maritime Sysadmin’s War Room
talks.teaser: Breaks down executive and technical incident response perspectives following real-world cyber incidents at the Marine Exchange of Southern California.
talks.summary:
The Crucial Role of Maritime Exchanges

The Marine Exchange of Southern California manages vessel traffic service and harbor safety across major seaport complexes, serving as an indispensable operational hub for maritime logistics.

Executive and Leadership Perspectives on Cyber Incidents

Executive Director Kit Louttit shares the strategic and operational considerations that arise during active cyber threats, focusing on stakeholder communication, business continuity, and maritime safety.

Firsthand Technical Incident Response in the War Room

Senior Systems Administrator Steve Winston breaks down the technical triage, log analysis, and rapid containment actions executed during incident response in the Marine Exchange's war room.

Building Resilient Maritime IT/OT Infrastructure

Lessons learned emphasize the necessity of cross-functional disaster recovery drills, robust network segmentation, and continuous monitoring to maintain harbor traffic services during critical outages.
